c74object.name: mqtt.client
c74object.description: Publishes and subscribes to MQTT topics. Other mqtt objects share its connection by name.

discussion.p: MQTT is a publish/subscribe protocol: clients publish messages to named topics on a broker, and every client subscribed to a matching topic receives them. Topics are paths such as studio/sensor/1; in subscribe, + matches one level and # all remaining levels.

mqtt.client speaks MQTT 3.1.1 through MQTT.js in a Node for Max process. Install its dependencies once per computer by sending script npm install. Messages sent before the process is ready, e.g. from a loadbang, are held and sent once it is.
Give the client a name to share its connection: mqtt.midi, mqtt.homie.device and mqtt.homie.controller with the same name use it. Without a name, the client works on its own.
Two clients with the same clientid disconnect each other: the broker closes the older connection. Leave it empty for a random one.
A password typed into the object box is saved in the patch in plain text. For anything other than a public test broker, send it with connect or a password message instead.

objarg.name: name
objarg.digest: Connection name shared with other mqtt objects

method.name: connect
method.description: Connects with the current attributes. With arguments, sets url, username and password first. URLs: mqtt://, mqtts:// (TLS), ws://, wss:// (WebSocket). Subscriptions are restored on every connection.

method.name: disconnect
method.description: Closes the connection cleanly. A connected mqtt.homie.device publishes its disconnected state first.

method.name: subscribe
method.description: Messages on topics matching the filter come out the left outlet. + matches one level, # the rest. QoS 0 (default), 1 or 2.

method.name: unsubscribe
method.description: Stops a subscription made with subscribe. Subscriptions of other mqtt objects on the same connection are not affected.

method.name: publish
method.description: Publishes the atoms as text, separated by spaces. A dictionary is published as JSON. Uses qos and retain. With retain 1 and no payload, deletes the retained message of the topic.

method.name: script
method.digest: Control the Node for Max process
method.description: Passed to node.script, e.g. script npm install once on a new computer.

attribute.name: url
attribute.description: The broker to connect to, e.g. mqtt://localhost:1883 or wss://broker.example.com:8884.

attribute.name: username
attribute.description: Login name, if the broker requires one.

attribute.name: password
attribute.description: Login password, if the broker requires one. Saved in the patch when typed into the object box.

attribute.name: clientid
attribute.description: The MQTT client identifier. Empty for a random one.

attribute.name: keepalive
attribute.description: Interval of keepalive messages. The broker considers the client gone after 1.5 times this interval without traffic, and publishes its last will.

attribute.name: clean
attribute.description: With 1, the broker discards the session when the client disconnects. With 0, it keeps subscriptions and queued QoS 1 and 2 messages for the same clientid.

attribute.name: qos
attribute.description: Quality of service for publish and publishbytes: 0 at most once, 1 at least once, 2 exactly once.

attribute.name: retain
attribute.description: With 1, the broker keeps the last message of each topic and sends it to new subscribers.

attribute.name: format
attribute.description: text: words and numbers. bytes: a list of byte values. json: a JSON object as a dictionary, anything else as text.

entry.name: left outlet
entry.description: Incoming messages: the topic followed by the payload, decoded by format.

entry.name: right outlet
entry.description: Dumpout: status connected, reconnecting or disconnected; error with a text; ready once the Node process runs; script messages from node.script.
